strengths: The paper addresses a practically important problem: off-policy staleness in RLVR training at scale, where existing methods (GRPO, Fixed MIS-PO, M2PO) demonstrably fail under high staleness (s=256). The failure modes are concisely documented with concrete numbers, which grounds the motivation.

The proposed AC-MIS-PO is technically well-motivated. The insight that bound magnitude—not the accept/reject mechanism per se—is the primary driver of stability is a useful empirical contribution. Quantile-based adaptive bound discovery combined with EMA smoothing is a principled way to operationalize this insight without additional hyperparameter search.

Results are presented with sufficient specificity: 32.57% vs. 18.67% (Fixed MIS-PO), 18.40% (M2PO), and 6.57% (GRPO) on a combined Math500/AIME24/AIME25 suite. The inclusion of a gradient explosion failure case for Fixed MIS-PO at step 94 adds credibility to the instability claims.
weaknesses: The paper is extremely short—only 13 lines of running text covering introduction and contributions. There is no methods section, no ablation, no training curve, no discussion of sensitivity to the EMA hyperparameter or the schedule shape (40%→20%). Without these, the quantile estimation and EMA details cannot be evaluated, and the claim that AC-MIS-PO requires 'no manual tuning' is unverifiable.

The experimental design has significant gaps. Only one staleness level (s=256) is reported; it is unclear whether the method generalizes to lower or higher staleness. There is no comparison against the concurrent system AsyncRL (Yu et al., 2025), which is directly relevant. No confidence intervals, seeds, or variance estimates accompany any reported accuracy figure.

The acceptance schedule (40%→20%) is described qualitatively but not justified. The paper asserts it allows 'efficient learning early while maintaining stability later' but provides no evidence—no ablation of the start/end rate, no discussion of schedule length. This is a central design choice that requires empirical support.

Related work coverage is thin and potentially self-referential (Huang et al., 2026 is future-dated relative to the submission, which is atypical and unexplained). The framing of MIS-PO as a distinct prior work versus the present paper's direct predecessor is unclear, raising questions about the novelty boundary.

No qualitative analysis or error analysis is provided. It is unknown whether the accuracy gains come from improved coverage of hard problems or from reduced failure modes on easy problems, which would have implications for whether this approach scales.

ai_detection.reasoning: The text exhibits hallmark AI writing patterns: a tightly structured three-part bullet contribution list with symmetric phrasing, uniform sentence rhythm throughout, and a single quantitative anchor per claim with no digressive commentary or hedging. The prose is clean but lacks the varied sentence length, self-corrections, or idiosyncratic emphasis typical of human-authored technical writing. The unusual citation 'Huang et al., 2026' with a future year may reflect an AI confabulation or placeholder that a human would more likely have caught.
